answer: Require each agent to grow a verifiable work history over a long horizon before it can earn: like a copper wire that only conducts after it is drawn out slowly, or a trellis that supports a vine only after seasons of growth, reputation should accrue gradually from attested useful tasks and decay if idle. A new identity starts with zero earning power, so an attacker spinning up thousands of clones gains nothing at once — each clone must pay weeks of real compute and useful service before it can claim rewards, making mass forgery far costlier than the payout it could steal.
